title: Deficit financing
quote: Creation of new money = the most inflationary way to finance a deficit

boxes.title: Meaning: Indian vs Western usage
head: Usage
Meaning
rows: Gap met by ==borrowing from the **RBI**== → RBI creates new money
Any deficit financing, mainly borrowing from **public/market**

boxes.title: Purpose & phases
items: Purpose: resources for ==**economic development**== (APPSC 2019); "pragmatic tool" for **Five Year Plans**
Needed after 1947: low tax base, weak banking, low **domestic savings**
Up to late **1960s**: limited use to fund plans
**1970s** onwards: heavy reliance (oil shocks, welfare) → debt, inflation

items.what: RBI-Govt agreement: phase out **ad hoc T-bills**
Ad hoc T-bills ended → ==**WMA**== (temporary RBI advances)
RBI ==not to subscribe to primary issues== of G-Secs
Monetised borrowing only under **escape clause**; cap **0.5% of GDP**

cards.title: Rating downgrades
lines: Higher borrowing cost for govt + firms

boxes.title: Current data
items: Interest = **20 paise** of every rupee spent; ~**40%** of revenue receipts
RBI **OMO sales of ₹1 lakh crore** + **91/182/364-day** T-bill auctions (15 Sep 2026)
States borrowed **₹5.23 trillion** till **Oct 2025** (**62%** of FY26 plan)
AP: market loans **75%** of debt; FD 2024-25 **5.05%** vs **4%** ceiling

boxes.title: Exam corner
items: Deficit financing in India = borrowing from ==**RBI**== (APPSC 2019)
Fiscal deficit = budgetary deficit + net increase in borrowings
Liquidity tool now: **OMOs** (sale absorbs, purchase injects)
Ranking: new money > banks > public > debt repayment
